title: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems
seo_title: Word Problems – Primary 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Solve word problems on addition and subtraction of numbers up to 100. (summary of the NERDC Primary 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction word problems up to 100: altogether, how many left, how many more and missing numbers. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the story. Find the numbers.
  • Altogether and in all mean add. Left and how many more mean subtract.
  • Write a number sentence and solve it.

Examples

Example

Ada has 35 sweets. She gives away 12. How many are left?

35 − 12

Answer: 23 sweets

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when things are taken awayLeft means take away.
Forgetting the unitWrite sweets, pupils or naira.
Using the wrong numbersUnderline the numbers.

items.q: Halima had 48 shells. She gave 37 shells to her brother. How many shells does Halima have now?
items.e: 37 were taken away, so subtract: 48 − 37 = ☐. 48 − 37 = 11. Answer: 11 shells.

items.q: A pet store had 61 fish in a tank. The store sold 26 fish. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: 26 were taken away, so subtract: 61 − 26 = ☐. 61 − 26 = 35. You cannot take 6 from 1 in the units place, so trade 1 ten for 10 units first. Answer: 35 fish.

items.q: There were 31 balloons at a party. Kemi blew up 29 more balloons. How many balloons are there now?
items.e: 29 more were added, so add: 31 + 29 = ☐. 31 + 29 = 60. Regroup: 1 + 9 = 10 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 60 balloons.

items.q: There were 16 people at the pool. Then 64 more people came. How many people are at the pool now?
items.e: 64 more were added, so add: 16 + 64 = ☐. 16 + 64 = 80. Regroup: 6 + 4 = 10 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 80 people.

items.q: Ms. Lee had 25 pencils. She bought 24 more pencils. How many pencils does Ms. Lee have now?
items.e: 24 more were added, so add: 25 + 24 = ☐. 25 + 24 = 49. Answer: 49 pencils.

items.q: Babatunde put 34 beads on a string. Then he added 59 more beads. How many beads are on the string now?
items.e: 59 more were added, so add: 34 + 59 = ☐. 34 + 59 = 93. Regroup: 4 + 9 = 13 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 93 beads.

items.q: A library cart had 60 books. Chinedu took 26 books off the cart. How many books are on the cart now?
items.e: 26 were taken away, so subtract: 60 − 26 = ☐. 60 − 26 = 34. You cannot take 6 from 0 in the units place, so trade 1 ten for 10 units first. Answer: 34 books.

items.q: Ngozi had 52 stickers. She gave 43 stickers to a friend. How many stickers does Ngozi have now?
items.e: 43 were taken away, so subtract: 52 − 43 = ☐. 52 − 43 = 9. You cannot take 3 from 2 in the units place, so trade 1 ten for 10 units first. Answer: 9 stickers.

items.q: Ruth had 89 marbles. She lost 33 marbles in a game. How many marbles does Ruth have now?
items.e: 33 were taken away, so subtract: 89 − 33 = ☐. 89 − 33 = 56. Answer: 56 marbles.

items.q: Zainab baked 35 biscuits. Her family ate 27 of the biscuits. How many biscuits are there now?
items.e: 27 were taken away, so subtract: 35 − 27 = ☐. 35 − 27 = 8. You cannot take 7 from 5 in the units place, so trade 1 ten for 10 units first. Answer: 8 biscuits.

items.q: There were 37 cars in a parking lot. Then 46 more cars came in. How many cars are in the lot now?
items.e: 46 more were added, so add: 37 + 46 = ☐. 37 + 46 = 83. Regroup: 7 + 6 = 13 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 83 cars.

items.q: Ikenna had 17 toy cars. For his birthday, he got 45 more toy cars. How many toy cars does Ikenna have now?
items.e: 45 more were added, so add: 17 + 45 = ☐. 17 + 45 = 62. Regroup: 7 + 5 = 12 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 62 toy cars.

items.q: There were 47 birds in a tree. 32 birds flew away. How many birds are in the tree now?
items.e: 32 were taken away, so subtract: 47 − 32 = ☐. 47 − 32 = 15. Answer: 15 birds.

items.q: There were 30 children on a bus. At the next stop, 11 children got off. How many children are on the bus now?
items.e: 11 were taken away, so subtract: 30 − 11 = ☐. 30 − 11 = 19. You cannot take 1 from 0 in the units place, so trade 1 ten for 10 units first. Answer: 19 children.

items.q: There were 19 ducks in a pond. Then 13 more ducks swam over. How many ducks are in the pond now?
items.e: 13 more were added, so add: 19 + 13 = ☐. 19 + 13 = 32. Regroup: 9 + 3 = 12 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 32 ducks.

items.q: A farm had 56 chickens. The farmer sold 32 chickens. How many chickens does the farm have now?
items.e: 32 were taken away, so subtract: 56 − 32 = ☐. 56 − 32 = 24. Answer: 24 chickens.

items.q: Sani had 36 apples in a basket. He picked 26 more apples. How many apples does Sani have now?
items.e: 26 more were added, so add: 36 + 26 = ☐. 36 + 26 = 62. Regroup: 6 + 6 = 12 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 62 apples.

items.q: A library cart had 23 books. Blessing put 47 more books on the cart. How many books are on the cart now?
items.e: 47 more were added, so add: 23 + 47 = ☐. 23 + 47 = 70. Regroup: 3 + 7 = 10 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 70 books.

items.q: Obinna had 64 shells. At the beach, he found 15 more shells. How many shells does Obinna have now?
items.e: 15 more were added, so add: 64 + 15 = ☐. 64 + 15 = 79. Answer: 79 shells.

items.q: There were 37 balloons at a party. Ibrahim blew up 16 more balloons. How many balloons are there now?
items.e: 16 more were added, so add: 37 + 16 = ☐. 37 + 16 = 53. Regroup: 7 + 6 = 13 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 53 balloons.

items.q: Ibrahim has 56 marbles. 25 are red, and the rest are blue. How many blue marbles does he have?
items.e: You know the whole (56) and one part (25). Find the other part: 25 + ☐ = 56, or 56 − 25 = ☐. 56 − 25 = 31. Answer: 31 marbles.

items.q: Yetunde bought 51 apples. 43 were green, and the rest were red. How many red apples did she buy?
items.e: You know the whole (51) and one part (43). Find the other part: 43 + ☐ = 51, or 51 − 43 = ☐. 51 − 43 = 8. Answer: 8 apples.

items.q: A pond has 60 ducks and geese. 37 of them are ducks. How many geese are on the pond?
items.e: You know the whole (60) and one part (37). Find the other part: 37 + ☐ = 60, or 60 − 37 = ☐. 60 − 37 = 23. Answer: 23 geese.

items.q: A farmer has 51 eggs. 42 are brown, and the rest are white. How many white eggs are there?
items.e: You know the whole (51) and one part (42). Find the other part: 42 + ☐ = 51, or 51 − 42 = ☐. 51 − 42 = 9. Answer: 9 eggs.

items.q: A bakery made 59 chocolate cupcakes and 24 vanilla cupcakes. How many cupcakes did it make?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 59 + 24 = ☐. 59 + 24 = 83. Answer: 83 cupcakes.

items.q: Kayode scored 19 points in the first game and 78 points in the second game. How many points did he score in all?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 19 + 78 = ☐. 19 + 78 = 97. Answer: 97 points.

items.q: A sticker sheet has 82 stars. 68 are gold, and the rest are silver. How many silver stars are there?
items.e: You know the whole (82) and one part (68). Find the other part: 68 + ☐ = 82, or 82 − 68 = ☐. 82 − 68 = 14. Answer: 14 stars.

items.q: Kelechi read 35 pages on Monday and Tuesday. He read 17 pages on Monday. How many pages did he read on Tuesday?
items.e: You know the whole (35) and one part (17). Find the other part: 17 + ☐ = 35, or 35 − 17 = ☐. 35 − 17 = 18. Answer: 18 pages.

items.q: A toy box has 36 toy cars and 19 toy trucks. How many toys are in the box?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 36 + 19 = ☐. 36 + 19 = 55. Answer: 55 toys.

items.q: A garden has 95 tulips. 23 are red, and the rest are yellow. How many yellow tulips are there?
items.e: You know the whole (95) and one part (23). Find the other part: 23 + ☐ = 95, or 95 − 23 = ☐. 95 − 23 = 72. Answer: 72 tulips.

items.q: An animal shelter has 18 cats and 15 dogs. How many animals are at the shelter?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 18 + 15 = ☐. 18 + 15 = 33. Answer: 33 animals.

items.q: A class planted 62 seeds. 49 were bean seeds, and the rest were corn seeds. How many corn seeds did the class plant?
items.e: You know the whole (62) and one part (49). Find the other part: 49 + ☐ = 62, or 62 − 49 = ☐. 62 − 49 = 13. Answer: 13 seeds.

items.q: A tree has 49 green leaves and 47 yellow leaves. How many leaves are on the tree?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 49 + 47 = ☐. 49 + 47 = 96. Answer: 96 leaves.

items.q: There are 49 girls and 31 boys at a school picnic. How many children are at the picnic?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 49 + 31 = ☐. 49 + 31 = 80. Answer: 80 children.

items.q: Nonso has 87 books. 63 are storybooks, and the rest are comic books. How many comic books does he have?
items.e: You know the whole (87) and one part (63). Find the other part: 63 + ☐ = 87, or 87 − 63 = ☐. 87 − 63 = 24. Answer: 24 comic books.

items.q: Kunle read 49 pages on Monday and 12 pages on Tuesday. How many pages did he read in all?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 49 + 12 = ☐. 49 + 12 = 61. Answer: 61 pages.

items.q: A pond has 24 ducks and 39 geese. How many birds are on the pond?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 24 + 39 = ☐. 24 + 39 = 63. Answer: 63 birds.

items.q: An animal shelter has 60 cats and dogs. 45 of them are cats. How many dogs are at the shelter?
items.e: You know the whole (60) and one part (45). Find the other part: 45 + ☐ = 60, or 60 − 45 = ☐. 60 − 45 = 15. Answer: 15 dogs.

items.q: Segun bought 37 green apples and 15 red apples. How many apples did he buy?
items.e: You know both parts. Put them together: 37 + 15 = ☐. 37 + 15 = 52. Answer: 52 apples.

items.q: A farmer has 89 eggs. 45 are brown, and the rest are white. How many white eggs are there?
items.e: You know the whole (89) and one part (45). Find the other part: 45 + ☐ = 89, or 89 − 45 = ☐. 89 − 45 = 44. Answer: 44 eggs.

items.q: There are 34 books on a shelf. Nonso puts 5 more books on the shelf. How many books are on the shelf now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Add the units: 4 + 5 = 9. The tens stay the same. 34 + 5 = 39.

items.q: Kayode has 46 marbles. He wins 7 more marbles. How many marbles does he have now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 46 + 4 = 50. 7 is 4 + 3, so add 3 more: 50 + 3 = 53.

items.q: A bus has 52 people on it. 8 people get off. How many people are still on the bus?
items.e: Some get off, so subtract. Go back to the ten first. 52 − 2 = 50. 8 is 2 + 6, so take away 6 more: 50 − 6 = 44.

items.q: There are 26 ducks on a pond. 9 more ducks land. How many ducks are there now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 26 + 4 = 30. 9 is 4 + 5, so add 5 more: 30 + 5 = 35.

items.q: Obinna has 63 stickers. He gives 30 stickers to his friend. How many stickers does he have left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 6 tens − 3 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 63 − 30 = 33.

items.q: One bus has 24 children on it. Another bus has 30 children. How many children are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 2 tens + 3 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: There are 81 children in the playground. 40 children go in for lunch. How many children are still in the playground?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 40 is 4 tens. Take away the tens: 8 tens − 4 tens = 4 tens. The ones stay the same. 81 − 40 = 41.

items.q: Temi has 7 red pencils, 5 blue pencils and 3 green pencils. How many pencils does she have?
items.e: Add all three numbers. Look for a number bond to 10: 7 + 3 = 10. Then 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: In a game, Uche scores 6 points, then 8 points, then 4 points. How many points does he score altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Look for a number bond to 10: 6 + 4 = 10. Then 10 + 8 = 18.

items.q: Kunle reads 35 pages on Monday and 42 pages on Tuesday. How many pages does he read altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Add the units: 5 + 2 = 7. Then 70 + 7 = 77.

items.q: A farmer has 47 sheep in one field and 38 sheep in another field. How many sheep are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Add the units: 7 + 8 = 15. Then 70 + 15 = 85.

items.q: A shop has 72 apples. It sells 25 apples. How many apples are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 72 − 20 = 52. Then take away 5. Go back to the ten: 52 − 2 = 50, then 50 − 3 = 47.

items.q: A bus has 40 seats. 26 people are sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Take the seats with people away from all the seats, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 40 − 20 = 20. Then take away the units: 20 − 6 = 14.

items.q: Bola has 45 marbles. Chinedu has 28 marbles. How many more marbles does Bola have than Chinedu?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 45 − 20 = 25. Then take away 8. Go back to the ten: 25 − 5 = 20, then 20 − 3 = 17.

items.q: There are 45 people on a bus. 8 people get off. Then 20 people get on. How many people are on the bus now?
Emeka has 58 beads. Abdullahi has 9 fewer beads than Emeka. How many beads does Abdullahi have?
items.e: Fewer means subtract. 58 − 8 = 50, then 50 − 1 = 49.

items.q: There are 34 books on a shelf. Usman puts 5 more books on the shelf. How many books are on the shelf now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Add the units: 4 + 5 = 9. The tens stay the same. 34 + 5 = 39.

items.q: Babatunde has 46 marbles. He wins 7 more marbles. How many marbles does he have now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 46 + 4 = 50. 7 is 4 + 3, so add 3 more: 50 + 3 = 53.

items.q: Halima has 63 stickers. She gives 30 stickers to her friend. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 6 tens − 3 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 63 − 30 = 33.

items.q: Funke has 7 red pencils, 5 blue pencils and 3 green pencils. How many pencils does she have?
items.e: Add all three numbers. Look for a number bond to 10: 7 + 3 = 10. Then 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: A page in Kelechi’s football sticker album holds 20 stickers. He has stuck in 13. How many more stickers does he need to fill the page?
Temi has 15 sweets. She eats 6. How many sweets are left?
items.e: She eats some, so subtract. 15 − 6 = 9. Check: 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q: There are 20 children on a bus. 8 children get off. How many children are still on the bus?
items.e: Children get off, so subtract. 20 − 8 = 12. Check: 12 + 8 = 20.

items.q: There are 12 children on a bus. 8 more get on. How many children are on the bus now?
items.e: More get on, so add. 2 + 8 = 10, so 12 + 8 = 20.

items.q: A box holds 10 eggs. There are 6 eggs in it. How many more eggs will fill the box?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10. So 4 eggs will fill the box.

items.q: A jigsaw has 100 pieces. Ikenna has put in 60 pieces. How many pieces are left?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10, so 60 + 40 = 100. 40 pieces are left.

items.q: Zainab has run 70 m of a 100 m race. How far is it to the finish?
items.e: 70 + 30 = 100. It is 30 m to the finish.

items.q: There are 20 pupils in a class. 11 are girls. How many are boys?
Yusuf has 7 red pencils and 8 blue pencils. How many pencils does he have?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 7 + 8 = 15. (1 is 8 − 7.)

items.q: Uju had some marbles. She gave away 5. Now she has 9. How many marbles did she have at first?
items.e: Use the inverse. Add back the 5 she gave away: 9 + 5 = 14. Check: 14 − 5 = 9.

items.q: Victor scores 6 points and then 9 points. Kayode scores 9 points and then 6 points. Who has more points?
items.e: 6 + 9 = 15 and 9 + 6 = 15. You can add in any order, so they have the same.

items.q: A plate has 16 biscuits. The children eat 9. How many biscuits are left?
Ngozi has 40 beads. She needs 100 beads for a necklace. How many more beads does she need?
items.e: 4 + 6 = 10, so 40 + 60 = 100. She needs 60 beads.

items.q: A car park has 100 spaces. 50 cars are parked. How many spaces are empty?
items.e: 5 + 5 = 10, so 50 + 50 = 100. 50 spaces are empty.

items.q: Dayo counts 14 people on the top deck of a bus. There are 20 seats. How many seats are empty?
items.e: 14 + 6 = 20. So 6 seats are empty.

items.q: Ngozi has 18 stickers. She gives 9 to her friend. How many stickers does she have now?

items.e: Start with 9. Take 1 from the 3 to make 10: 9 + 1 = 10. Then add the 2 left: 10 + 2 = 12.
Think addition: 9 + 8 = 17. So 17 − 9 = 8.
Think addition: 3 + 8 = 11. So 11 − 3 = 8.
Start with 8. Take 2 from the 4 to make 10: 8 + 2 = 10. Then add the 2 left: 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Nneka says 74 − 38 = 44. Is she right?
items.e: Check by adding: 44 + 38 = 82, not 74. So 44 is wrong. Units: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 14 − 8 = 6. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. Answer: 36. Check: 36 + 38 = 74.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 71 − ☐ = 28
items.e: Think: 71 take away what number leaves 28? Find 71 − 28. Units: 1 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 11 − 8 = 3. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 43. Check: 71 − 43 = 28.

items.q: Gbenga says 91 − 56 = 35. Is he right?
items.e: Check by adding: 35 + 56 = 91. You get back 91, so he is right. Units: 1 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 11 − 6 = 5. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. Answer: 35.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 15 = 72
items.e: Use subtraction: 72 − 15 = ☐. Units: 2 − 5 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 12 − 5 = 7. Tens: 6 − 1 = 5. Answer: 57. Check: 57 + 15 = 72.

items.q: What is 40 − 16?
items.e: Units: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 24. Check: 24 + 16 = 40. Or count up: 16 + 4 = 20, then 20 + 20 = 40. 4 + 20 = 24.

items.q: What is 90 − 55?
items.e: Units: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 10 − 5 = 5. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 55 = 90. Or count up: 55 + 5 = 60, then 60 + 30 = 90. 5 + 30 = 35.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 24 + ☐ = 72
items.e: Use subtraction: 72 − 24 = ☐. Units: 2 − 4 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 12 − 4 = 8. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 48. Check: 24 + 48 = 72.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 43 = 91
items.e: Use subtraction: 91 − 43 = ☐. Units: 1 − 3 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 11 − 3 = 8. Tens: 8 − 4 = 4. Answer: 48. Check: 48 + 43 = 91.

items.q: Nonso found 64 − 29 = 35. Which addition checks his answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 35 + 29 = 64. You get back 64, so the answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Units: 0 − 4 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 8 − 3 = 5. Answer: 56. Check: 56 + 34 = 90. Or count up: 34 + 6 = 40, then 40 + 50 = 90. 6 + 50 = 56.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Units: 0 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 10 − 7 = 3. Tens: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 23. Check: 23 + 37 = 60. Or count up: 37 + 3 = 40, then 40 + 20 = 60. 3 + 20 = 23.

items.q: Blessing found 81 − 47 = 34. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 34 + 47 = 81. You get back 81, so the answer is right.

items.q: Samuel found 72 − 35 = 37. Which addition checks his answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 37 + 35 = 72. You get back 72, so the answer is right.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 18 + ☐ = 67
items.e: Use subtraction: 67 − 18 = ☐. Units: 7 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 17 − 8 = 9. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 49. Check: 18 + 49 = 67.

items.q: Joy says 63 − 28 = 45. Is she right?
items.e: Check by adding: 45 + 28 = 73, not 63. So 45 is wrong. Units: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 28 = 63.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 24 = 73
items.e: Use subtraction: 73 − 24 = ☐. Units: 3 − 4 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 13 − 4 = 9. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 49. Check: 49 + 24 = 73.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 55 − ☐ = 26
items.e: Think: 55 take away what number leaves 26? Find 55 − 26. Units: 5 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 15 − 6 = 9. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 29. Check: 55 − 29 = 26.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Units: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 10 − 2 = 8. Tens: 8 − 2 = 6. Answer: 68. Check: 68 + 22 = 90. Or count up: 22 + 8 = 30, then 30 + 60 = 90. 8 + 60 = 68.

items.q: What is 100 − 46?
items.e: 100 is 10 tens. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: now 9 tens and 10 units. Units: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 54. Check: 54 + 46 = 100. Or count up: 46 + 4 = 50, then 50 + 50 = 100. 4 + 50 = 54.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 53 − ☐ = 27
items.e: Think: 53 take away what number leaves 27? Find 53 − 27. Units: 3 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 units: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 26. Check: 53 − 26 = 27.
